So he sees himself as an enlightened individualist. To paraphrase- someone who doesn’t judge based on race, religion or any other form of group identity.

These people are not an ignorable minority, in fact they characterize the only other acceptable camp of thought present now in the West.

This may be an accurate assessment of Peterson's thoughts. He doesn't seem very deep to me. But it doesn't mean that it's an accurate assessment of "individualism." A belief that all human beings are rootless atoms is the ultimate, inescapable univeralism. It's a collectivism of last resort after all other attempts have failed. It is not individualism as any right-thinking person understands it, and these writers do it and themselves a disservice confusing two same things for opposing things.

Individualism means taking your moral principles with you, incorporating it into your being, and using only that as your guide and reference. This is as opposed to the weak-willed knee-benders who seek external validation, whose principles are fluid, and who require consensus to act. Individualism means independence. It means being and knowing how to be, and admitting that the human being has limits which require knowing these things in the first place. It can be selfish and isolated. It can be rootless or steeped in heritage. It encompasses pioneering, invention, and even laziness.

I've noticed this trend against a straw-man of "individualism" in a couple of places recently, and one is the lightweights of the self-styled "alt right." Another is lightweight critics of "the alt right" in certain orthodoxy religious publications. They pretend to oppose each other, and yet argue for the making same error in favor of an orthodox authority which they are part of. Neither seem to understand the roots of their ideology in the least, or they would understand legitimate authority and the meaning of carrying it with you.
